I will analyze wb_page1_2001_2010.csv using the criterion: all 10 years >35% and no missing values.
I’ll also exclude aggregates using a heuristic (remove names containing 'World', '&', or parentheses).
```python
import pandas as pd
wide = pd.read_csv('wb_page1_2001_2010.csv')
years = [str(y) for y in range(2001,2011)]
# Coerce numeric
for y in years:
    wide[y] = pd.to_numeric(wide[y], errors='coerce')
# basic aggregate filter
def is_country(name):
    bad_tokens = ['World', 'income', 'IBRD', 'IDA', 'OECD', 'Euro area', '(']
    return not any(t in name for t in bad_tokens)
wide = wide[wide['country'].apply(is_country)]
# qualify function
def qualifies(row):
    vals = row[years]
    return vals.notnull().all() and (vals > 35).all()
cands = wide[wide.apply(qualifies, axis=1)]['country'].tolist()
print('candidates_on_page1:', cands)
```
